chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: Bill Pemberton asks about the Teddy Wilson sessions
summary: Pemberton asks about mixing men from different orchestras, and Jones says they were just trying to get a point across, not be commercial.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Can I ask you a question?
Later on we had called the Roseland and there then were some dates. As you know, you played on the dates because we were out of town.
1937. You were down at the Cotton Club.
I was at the Cotton Club with Cab Calloway.
What did you make with her?
Don't look for it if it isn't there because this is a matter of record.
All right, I got the records. You know I'm going to get to that later on.
Bill wants to ask you something.

I wanted to ask, at that particular time you had things that were happening, for instance, like with the Benny Goodman group that was together, that they had also Teddy playing. Also records were being made with people from different orchestras. Did that have anything to do with this? You know, at the time that Teddy had the orchestra and then he just used... men from...?

No, the idea of it was, Bill, at that time it could have been your group. It could have been Milt's group. It could have been mine. All we were interested in - we weren't thinking commercial, we were thinking about just

trying to get a point across to the American public and to the world in general of what we were trying to do. We came from all left field. You had different kind of peoples came in just to be on the recording session, just to do something for posterity.
